newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca profits top 1 billion pounds ($1.6 billion).
newsitem.headline: Zeneca profits top 1 billion pounds ($1.6 billion).

text.p: Zeneca Group Plc, Britain's third-largest drug company, broke through the billion-pound pre-tax profit barrier Tuesday, propelled by strong growth in pharmaceuticals and agricultural chemicals.
The bioscience group said 1996 pre-tax profit before exceptional charges soared to 1.011 billion pounds ($1.6 billion), above the top end of analysts' forecasts.

The company's 13 percent rise in sales to 2.44 billion pounds ($3.9 billion) dwarfed the 6 percent rise reported by Glaxo Wellcome Plc last week. Operating profit on pharmaceutical sales rose 10 percent to 757 million pounds ($1.2 billion) from 687 million ($1.1 billion).

Growth was driven by sales of cardiovascular drug Zestril, which rose 10 percent despite increased competition. Sales of established prostate cancer drug Zoladex rose 31 percent and newly launched prostate cancer drug Casodex "exceeded expectations" with sales of 68 million pounds ($109 million).
The company also announced the approval of its new migraine drug Zomig, acquired from Glaxo Wellcome Plc, in the United Kingdom.

Looking ahead, Zeneca said it expected further "strong volume growth" in 1997, but warned that market development and launch costs for new drugs and chemicals "will continue to restrain short-term profit growth, but should significantly enhance the long-term prospects of the group."
